To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we characterized the molecular and synaptic identity of a novel class of layer 5 neurons of the primary sensory cortex that provide direct monosynaptic projections to the spinal dorsal gray matter.

cholecystokin (CCK) expressing layer 5 pyramids of the mouse primary somatosensary cortex (S1) innervate the spinal dorsal horn and that these neurons are heterogeneous in their molecular composition.

we characterized the molecular and functional properties of CCK positive neurons in layer 5 of the primary somatic sensory cortex and that we identified these neurons as a major source for descending input to the spinal cord.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the neuronal circuits of the spinal cord dorsal horn, in particular with the role of cortical input.
the characterization of a major descending pathway to the dorsal spinal cord, the S1 CST neurons.
the identification of neuronal circuits that are involved in the processing of somatosensory information at the level of the spinal cord and with the elucidation of their function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CCK+ S5 CST neurons constitute a novel population of cortical neurons projecting to the spinal dorsal hom.
CCK positive S1 CST neurons are a major source of descending input to the spinal cord.
the S1 CST neurons are a heterogeneous population that is characterized by distinct molecular features, and which receives input from different sources in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CCK+ S 1CST neurons represent a novel population of cortical projection neurons with distinct molecular subgroups that are monosynaptically connected to layer 2/ 3 pyramidal cells and to thalamus and that provide excitatory input to inhibitory interneurons and excitatory projection neurons in the spinal cord.
the primary somatosensation cortex sends a heterogeneous population of neurons to the dorsal spinal cord that are likely involved in sensory processing and modulation.
CCK+ S2 CST neurons are a heterogeneous population of neurons with a wide range of inputs and target neurons in the dorsal horn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CCK+ S 1 CST neurons are a major source of cortical input to the spinal cord and that they are heterogeneous in their molecular composition.
S1 CST projections are not a homogeneous population but a complex network with distinct molecular subtypes and distinct synaptic targets in the dorsal spinal cord.
CCK+ S5 neurons constitute a major source of cortical input to the spinal cord, which is likely to play a role in the processing of somatosensory information.
